transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Yeah, um... what brings me in is I just can't seem to keep my words in a straight line anymore. It's like... I'll start talking about an overnight shift. I work as an orderly, and the nights get really long, especially when it's quiet and you can just hear the vending machine humming down the hall. It makes this weird buzzing noise. But yeah, I'll try to tell someone about work, and suddenly I end up jumping to soccer. I played soccer back in high school, mostly on defense. Our jerseys were this really intense shade of blue. Which is funny, because the paint colors on the walls at the hospital are supposed to be calming, you know? Like this pale, washed-out green. But I'll be talking about the paint colors, and then suddenly I'm rambling about patient charts, and... I don't know, I just look at people's faces while I'm talking and I can see everyone getting completely lost. I just can't hold on to the point of what I'm trying to say.
Beyond these difficulties with your speech, have you been experiencing any prolonged periods where your mood feels unusually elevated or, conversely, extremely low?

Yeah, um... low. Extremely low. Most days I just feel so heavy and completely empty right from the time I wake up. It's hard to even get moving. Like, after my shifts at the hospital, I'll just sit out in my car crying for a long time before I can even bring myself to drive home. I usually park in the employee lot, near the back by the dumpsters, because the front row fills up so fast by the time I get there. The seagulls always hang around those dumpsters. It's weird because we're not even that close to the ocean, but there are always seagulls out there. They make that awful screeching sound. I tried throwing them a piece of a granola bar once, the oats and honey kind, but they didn't even want it. They just want the garbage. I used to eat those granola bars every single day in high school. My locker was right next to the cafeteria doors, so it always smelled like tater tots... wait, what did you ask me? About my mood? Yeah, just... crying in my car. Really empty.
Have you ever had experiences where you heard, saw, or believed things that others around you did not, even during times when your mood was relatively stable and not feeling so low?

Yeah... yeah, I have. Um, actually, a little while ago, there was this stretch of a few weeks where I wasn't really feeling that deep, heavy sadness. Like, I wasn't crying in the car or anything. But even then... I still knew the cameras at work were watching me. Like, specifically me. And the supervisors, too, they were monitoring everything I did. I had to be so careful and guarded all the time. Which is exhausting, you know? Because the cameras are those little black domes on the ceiling. There's one right above the supply closet where we keep the extra linens and the, um, the non-slip socks. Those socks are always yellow or gray. I wore a pair once when I had to get my appendix out when I was sixteen. The hospital food was terrible, mostly just this weird red Jell-O. I hate Jell-O. The texture is just... it's like eating a rubber band. My mom used to make it with fruit suspended inside it for potlucks. She had this special Tupperware mold for it. It was seafoam green... but yeah, even when I wasn't feeling so low, I still knew they were monitoring me at work.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt unusually energetic, didn't need much sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing, even if you weren't feeling sad?

No, um... no, I've never really felt like that. I'm pretty much always just exhausted. I don't think I've ever had a time where I didn't need sleep. I'm usually trying to get more sleep, especially because the coffee in the breakroom at work is so terrible. They have this machine that uses those little plastic pods, but whoever does the ordering keeps getting the decaf ones with the orange foil on top. I don't know why anyone would want decaf on a night shift. But orange is just... it's a really loud color, you know? Like those traffic cones they set up when they do road work on the highway. The reflective tape on them always catches my headlights when I'm driving home in the dark. My car's headlights are actually getting kind of dim, I think I need to replace the bulbs soon. But you have to take the whole front bumper off just to get to the plastic housing for the bulb, which is such a stupid design. My uncle used to be a mechanic and he'd always complain about how cars are built these days, how everything is just cheap plastic clips that snap off if you pull them wrong... um... but yeah, no. I don't get energetic or have racing thoughts like that. I just sleep whenever I can.
